title: Describe the Data Using the Median
objective: I can find the median of a data set and use it to describe what is typical.
model: ordered list / dot plot where the median is the middle value found by counting in from both ends (mean of the two middle values for an even count)

widgets.component: Warm-up on histogram bars and intervals (lesson 2-2)
widgets.root: Matches the lesson's own warm-up (bar height 6, interval width 10, total from bar heights 17, histogram vs bar graph). Keys verified.

widgets.where: Practice §2 items 1, 4, 5 (2 mc find the mean, 1 err 'forgot to divide')
widgets.component: Find the mean of 10, 14, 8, 12, 16 / 6, 8, 10, 12, 14; Mean Mistake
widgets.root: Computing a mean (sum ÷ count) is the content of lesson 2-8; 2-3's key idea, objective and vocabulary are median, mode and outlier. Three of the five 'Practice with support' items are mean items, so the guided section for the median lesson contains one median item.
widgets.replacement: Replace with median/mode-only items on the same skills, same structure: a find-the-median mc on 5 unordered values (answer needs ordering first), a find-the-mode mc, and an error-analysis item where the student averaged the two middle values of an ODD count or skipped ordering. Do not print 'sum ÷ count' anywhere in this lesson.

widgets.component: Find the median of 3, 7, 2, 9, 5 (unordered) and the mode of 4, 7, 4, 9, 2, 4, 8
widgets.root: Both are the lesson's skills; the unordered median list traps 'middle of the list as written' (choice 3 vs 5).

widgets.component: Mean, median and mode of three sets; match mean / median / mode / range to definitions
widgets.root: Mean ('Sum ÷ Count') and range ('Max − Min') are taught in 2-8 and 2-5; the Mean column is 3 of the 9 table cells and 2 of the 4 match pairs ask for mean or range.
widgets.replacement: Table: three data sets (one odd count, one even count, one with an outlier) with columns Ordered list, Median, Mode only. Match: median / mode / outlier / typical value to their descriptions.

widgets.where: Practice §3 items 3-4 (mc even-count median, err even-count median)
widgets.component: Median of 4, 6, 6, 8, 10, 12 and the one-middle-value mistake
widgets.root: Even-count median (6 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7 and the 10-vs-12 error fix are right; it is the lesson's even-count step.

widgets.component: Generated medians: ordered odd list, unordered odd/even list, median from a dot plot or table
widgets.root: Sampled 120 seeds per level: L1 ordered odd lists, L2 mixed odd/even unordered, L3 dot plot or frequency table with an odd/even count; the keys follow ordering and middle-pair averaging.

widgets.component: Build the chart: tick values off a table and stack dots
widgets.root: The student stacks one dot per table value; the table ticks values off so the task is transcription, and it never asks for the median, the lesson's skill.
widgets.replacement: After the dot plot is built, add a Step 2: 'Cross off the least and greatest dot, then the next pair, until one dot (or two) remain; tap the median.' Grade the final tap (odd count: that dot; even count: tap between the two and type their mean), and trap the student who taps the tallest stack (mode).

widgets.component: 'The teacher said most students scored around 87', 'the most common score was 92', 'median of the 10 scores'
widgets.root: None of the three has the data. The lesson's Connect dot plot (85, 92, 78, 88, 92, 95, 72, 88, 92, 84) and quote were dropped, so '10 scores' cannot be found. 5.1 also asks the student to recognise a mean (866 ÷ 10).
widgets.replacement: Attach the Connect dot plot (viz dots, min 70, max 100, step 5, label 'Quiz score') to 5.1-5.3. Rewrite 5.1 as 'A student says "most students scored around 88." Which measure is that?' (median, 88 = (88 + 88) ÷ 2), keep 5.2 (mode 92) and 5.3 (median 88).

widgets.component: Median and what it tells you; six scans; median given, find the fifth score
widgets.root: Keys verified (4, 7, 7, 10, 12 gives 7; 41 and 45 give 43; fifth score 14).

widgets.component: Median with unordered lists, dot plots/tables, a new value added, a missing number
widgets.root: L4 'median of 5 numbers is 26; missing number' has a unique answer; 'a new value is added' re-ranks the list.

widgets.where: Challenge §2 items 1-3 (err mean/median/mode, wr mean vs median, tbl mean and median)
widgets.component: Find the Stats Error; typical game with an outlier; mean and median table
widgets.root: All three require adding and dividing (16, 21, 11.6, 19.2). The mean is not yet taught, so these items have students compute a mean in order to criticise it.
widgets.replacement: Replace with median/mode-only items on the same skills, same structure: a find-the-median mc on 5 unordered values (answer needs ordering first), a find-the-mode mc, and an error-analysis item where the student averaged the two middle values of an ODD count or skipped ordering. Do not print 'sum ÷ count' anywhere in this lesson. For the outlier comparison use median vs the largest value and mode, e.g. 'which better describes a typical game: the median, 16, or the maximum, 42?'

widgets.component: Median of 9 witness times, 6 footprints, six alibi checks with an outlier, add a sixth score
widgets.root: Keys verified: 11, 25.5, 30.5, 12.5. 2.6's distractor mentions the mean as a wrong choice but the keyed reasoning is about the median.

widgets.where: Challenge §3 items 1-2 (act:dotbalance goal median L3, goal outlier L4)
widgets.component: Balance the dots: move dots so the median stays, then move the outlier so the mean equals the median
widgets.root: dotbalance draws a mean triangle under the beam and shows a live mean readout in every goal; the median puzzle must also satisfy 'mean above K' and the outlier puzzle's goal is 'mean = median'. The mean (2-8) and mean-vs-median reasoning (2-10) are not yet taught.
widgets.replacement: Add a goal 'median-only' to assets/studio-act/dotbalance.js: hide the mean triangle and the mean readout; the student drags dots so the median reads a stated target (e.g. 6) and then so it does NOT change when the largest dot is dragged right (trapping 'the biggest value moves the middle'); readouts: median and the count of dots left/right of it.

widgets.component: Is the median one of the numbers or between two numbers
widgets.root: Odd counts sort to 'in the set', even counts to 'between'; verified all six cards.

widgets.component: Detective items (unordered, even count, odd count averaged), outlier 40 to 400, medians of 7 and 10 values, dot plot median, 'must be true', write-your-own
widgets.root: Each err item is a lesson misconception (not ordered; pick one of two middle values; average for an odd count); 5.4 x = 20 and 5.5 'at least half' verified.
